terminalBench.provenance: Per-task commits resolved from harbor-framework/harbor registry.json@v0.22.0 dataset terminal-bench@2.0 (the legacy-registry corpus the official runner used via `harbor run -d terminal-bench@2.0`); all 21 corpus tasks resolve to this single snapshot commit. The eval repo's tasks/ copies are public metadata only: they carry no tests/ and their [agent] timeouts, [environment] env/allow_internet fields diverge from what actually ran.

deepSwe.provenance: DEEP_SWE_REF default of the official skill's provision-golden-checkpoint.sh (benchmark.json reproduction_ref is a corrupted transcription of this sha). The -v1.1 separate-verifier images at this ref are the reproduction-correct environments and differ from the frozen public task metadata for three tasks.

specificationGaps.note: Diagnostic classification only. A task listed here was attempted exactly once under the frozen corpus and its canonical verdict stands unchanged; the record says that its pinned instruction never states a rule its hidden tests require, so its outcome cannot be read as a capability measurement and is excluded from capability comparisons. Nothing here rewrites an instruction, changes the corpus, or re-runs a task: the pinned instruction bytes stay exactly as the source froze them, and the only fix for a gap is an upstream task revision that re-freezes the corpus.

tasks.omission: The instruction requires a continuation line to append to the previous header value but never states how the fold is normalized.
tasks.observed: One fail-to-pass case failed on the fold: a HTAB-indented continuation was kept as written instead of unfolding to a single SP.

tasks.omission: The instruction states nearest-wins precedence and that include_router parameters apply to omitted values, but never states what an include_router call does to a value that an inner include_router call already resolved.
tasks.observed: One fail-to-pass case failed on a three-level include_router chain: an outer include_router value overrode a value an inner include_router call had already resolved.

tasks.omission: The instruction says for-of heads accept using and await using, but never states how a head is disambiguated when the binding itself is named of.
tasks.observed: One fail-to-pass case failed on that disambiguation: the head did not parse as a using-declaration with of as its binding name.
